# Lab 4.6: Dates, Times & Time Series

## What We Are Going to Do
Work with time zones, INTERVAL and RANGE values, and build a regular time series with TIMESTAMP_BUCKET and GAP_FILL.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Time zones.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() AS utc_now,
  DATETIME(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), 'Asia/Kolkata') AS india_now,
  TIMESTAMP('2026-11-09 09:00:00', 'Asia/Kolkata') AS ist_as_utc,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%d %b %Y %H:%M', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), 'Asia/Kolkata') AS pretty;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] INTERVAL and RANGE.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 10:00:00' + INTERVAL 90 MINUTE AS plus_90m,
  DATE '2026-03-31' + INTERVAL 1 MONTH AS next_month,
  RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-02-01'),
                 RANGE(DATE '2026-01-15', DATE '2026-03-01')) AS overlaps,
  RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-12-31'), DATE '2026-06-01') AS contains;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Bucket events into 6-hour windows.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT TIMESTAMP_BUCKET(created_at, INTERVAL 6 HOUR) AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`
WHERE created_at &gt;= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 3 DAY)
GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY bucket;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[SQL] Fill gaps in a time series.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TEMP TABLE readings AS
SELECT * FROM UNNEST([
  STRUCT(TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS ts, 10.0 AS temp),
  (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:03:00', 13.0),
  (TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:05:00', 15.0)]);

SELECT * FROM GAP_FILL(
  TABLE readings,
  ts_column =&gt; 'ts',
  bucket_width =&gt; INTERVAL 1 MINUTE,
  value_columns =&gt; [('temp', 'linear')]
)
ORDER BY ts;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Run the statements in this step together as one script. Minutes 1, 2 and 4 are filled in by linear interpolation.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| TIMESTAMP | Stored in UTC, shown in any zone |
| `RANGE_OVERLAPS` | `true` |
| `TIMESTAMP_BUCKET` | Regular 6-hour buckets |
| `GAP_FILL` | Missing minutes filled (11, 12, 14) |
